Basic information: 57-year-old patient referred for surgical consult due to melanoma on the back. Biopsy confirmed melanoma.

History of present illness: Melanoma was identified on the right inferior back, approximately 0.7 millimeters in size. The patient did not experience pain or itching. The lesion was noticed by the patient's mother during a visit last month, prompting a dermatological evaluation and subsequent biopsy. The biopsy showed it was a malignant melanoma, invasive, with a Breslow thickness of 0.7 millimeters and a Clark level 4. It was a superficial spreading type, with no ulceration or lymphatic invasion identified. The patient has not noticed any changes in the lesion since it was first identified. The patient has a slightly abnormal lymph node in the right groin, and an ultrasound is planned to evaluate for potential lymph node involvement. The ultrasound of the right groin lymph node has not been performed yet, and the patient does not know when it is scheduled. The patient has not undergone any other imaging studies or blood work for staging the melanoma. No sentinel lymph node biopsies or other staging procedures have been performed yet.

Past history: The patient has no history of other cancers or chronic conditions. He has had prior surgeries for gallbladder and appendectomy. There is a family history of melanoma (mother and maternal aunt). The patient is unsure about HPV vaccination status. He has significant sun exposure due to his occupation at an auto repair shop, uses sunscreen, and has never used tanning beds. He has annual mole checks by his primary care physician with no prior concerning findings.
